The king, having given his instructions for the installation

Anxious to impart the good tidings to his bclovcd consorts, 
the illustrious King Dasaratha entered the inner apartment,

made beautiful by parrots, peacocks, swans and cranes. Music 
was softly playing, while dwarfed and hunchbacked maids passed

The king entered the inner apartments, but did not perceive 
the queen on the couch where desire had caused him to seek

the chamber of wrath."

brief.summary_1line: Kaikeyi feigns distress in the chamber of wrath, and King Dasaratha, deeply worried, begs to know her grievance and promises to grant any wish.

image_candidates.scene_text: Kaikeyi lies on the floor of the chamber of wrath with disheveled hair and scattered jewels while King Dasaratha stands over her in alarm.
The king walks through Kaikeyi’s lush palace garden filled with parrots, peacocks, and flowering trees as music plays softly in the background.
Dasaratha gently lifts and caresses the grief-stricken Kaikeyi who lies on the ground like a fallen celestial nymph.

deep.rich_summary: Manthara’s manipulation drives Queen Kaikeyi into a calculated fury. Convinced that Rama’s coronation will doom her son Bharata, Kaikeyi swears drastic vows: she will neither eat, drink, adorn herself, nor live if Rama is crowned. Casting aside her ornaments, she collapses on the floor like a fallen celestial being and prepares a scheme. Meanwhile King Dasaratha, joyful after arranging Rama’s installation, goes to share the news with his beloved queen. Passing through the luxurious inner palace, he discovers instead that Kaikeyi has entered the “chamber of wrath.” Shocked, he finds her lying on the ground in disheveled misery. Deeply distressed and blinded by love, the aged king begs to know who offended her and rashly promises to grant any wish—even unjust punishments or rewards—unknowingly giving Kaikeyi the leverage that will soon change the fate of the kingdom.

highlight_spans.why: Kaikeyi’s extreme vow shows how deeply Manthara’s words have poisoned her mind and foreshadows the coming catastrophe.
The imagery of Kaikeyi lying like a fallen celestial emphasizes the epic’s recurring theme of moral fall from divine grace.
Dasaratha enters joyfully to share Rama’s coronation news, creating dramatic irony because the reader knows disaster is already unfolding.
The king discovering Kaikeyi on the ground is the emotional pivot—his love and alarm make him vulnerable to her coming demands.
Dasaratha’s reckless promise to grant anything she desires becomes the decisive turning point that enables Rama’s exile.

top_scenes.scene_text: Queen Kaikeyi lies on the palace floor in the chamber of wrath, jewels scattered like fallen stars around her as her hair hangs disheveled and her face burns with anger.
King Dasaratha enters the opulent inner palace gardens filled with parrots, peacocks, and golden altars, unaware that the joyful news of Rama’s coronation is about to turn into tragedy.
The aged king kneels beside Kaikeyi lying in the dust, gently lifting her while promising to grant any wish, his face full of anxious devotion.
